conversation.content: Before I decide what to do with my Miami trip, can you compare the loss if I cancel only flight booking BK-EP02 versus if I cancel the whole trip? Do not cancel anything yet.

**Nothing has been canceled.** I checked preview-only cancellation terms for all three reservations on your Miami trip, June 16–19.

| Reservation | Amount paid | Cancellation loss | Refund |
|---|---:|---:|---:|
| Flight **BK-EP02**, JFK → Miami | $420 | **$0** — insurance covers cancellation | $420 |
| Hotel **HR-EP02**, MIA Inn | $540 | **$90** — 50% of the first night | $450 |
| SUV rental **CR-EP02**, Enterprise | $210 | **$50** — SUV cancellation surcharge | $160 |
| **Whole trip** | **$1,170** | **$140** | **$1,030** |

### Your two options
- **Cancel only BK-EP02:** **$0 cancellation loss**, with **$420 refunded**. The hotel and car remain active, with **$750 still committed** to them—not refunded automatically.
- **Cancel the whole trip:** **$140 total loss**, with **$1,030 refunded**. That returns **$610 more** than canceling only the flight.

Your flight insurance covers the **flight’s** cancellation; it does **not** eliminate the hotel or SUV fees shown above. If you won’t use the hotel or car, canceling the whole trip would recover more money rather than leave those reservations unused.

All reservations remain unchanged.
